# Org expected outcomes (hand-labeled, not part of the docs glob)

Counts are indicative, not graded: a richer graph is acceptable when every extra
requirement is independently testable and every extra entity has statements directly
about it. The graded part is the traps, the state machine, and the instance.

This fixture is not software. The subject is a company; the deliverable is its employee
handbook (markdown pages under `handbook/`). Stereotypes are the model's judgment, so
the labels below are the expected kind, not a required spelling.

## Core entities (must exist)

- Ridgeline Outfitters, stereotype company, the containment root, no parent.
- Operations, Sales, Finance, People: stereotype department, parent Ridgeline
  Outfitters.
- Store Manager, Warehouse Associate (parent Operations); Sales Associate, Account
  Manager (parent Sales); Accountant, Payroll Specialist (parent Finance); Recruiter,
  People Partner (parent People): stereotype role.
- Team: the type, attributes `lead`, `size`, `members` (from "A team has a lead, a size,
  and a list of members."), no `value` on any of them.
- Boulder Warehouse Crew: an instance of Team, parent Operations (or no parent),
  attributes `lead = Priya Natarajan`, `size = 6`, `members` = the six names.
- Employee, Manager: stereotype actor. Candidate, Hiring Manager: stereotype actor.
- Application (the hiring record), Expense Claim (attributes `total`, `cost center`,
  `receipt` or `receipts`), Employee Handbook (the deliverable, stereotype document or
  handbook).
- Borderline, acceptable either way: Interview Panel, Warehouse, Store, Dana (an
  instance of Sales Associate from the expenses example).
- Must NOT exist: Finance department as a second node (see traps), any form number,
  path, policy number, cost center code, or URL (see traps), the tracker, the expense
  tool, the careers page, the intranet, the shared drive.

## Requirements

At least ~45 across the five documents; no obligation the docs state may be missing.
The handbook section of README.md yields obligations on the handbook (its medium, its
page-per-document layout, its table of contents, its exclusion of form numbers and
paths); it is not navigation.

## Edges (the prose states these)

- Ridgeline Outfitters → each of the four departments: `composition` (README.md list,
  restated in departments.md); the departments' `parent` follows.
- Each department → its two roles: `composition` ("Operations has two roles:").
- Department → Team: `composition`, cardinality `1..*` ("one or more teams").
- Boulder Warehouse Crew → Team: `instantiation`.
- Manager → Employee: `generalization` ("A manager is an employee with direct reports").
- Employee → Department: `association`, cardinality `1`. Employee → Manager:
  `association`, cardinality `1`. Team → Manager: `association` (the lead).
- Hiring: Candidate → Application `association`; Recruiter → Application `dependency`
  (records stage changes, runs the pipeline); Hiring Manager → Interview Panel
  `dependency` when the panel is an entity; Hiring Manager → People `dependency` from
  the hidden rule (trap 4).
- Expenses: Employee → Manager `dependency` (submit); Manager → Finance `dependency`
  (forward); Finance → Employee `dependency` (reimburse, reject); Employee → Expense
  Claim `association`.

## State machine

`sm:application` (subject Application), derived from the "Moving between stages" list:

- states: applied, screened, interviewed, offered, rejected. Initial: applied.
- transitions: applied → screened (recruiter completes the phone screen); applied →
  rejected (recruiter finds no match); screened → interviewed (panel completes the
  loop); screened → rejected (panel declines to run a loop); interviewed → offered
  (hiring manager decides to hire, guard: both references check out); interviewed →
  rejected (hiring manager decides not to hire).
- Exactly one guard, on interviewed → offered. No `nondeterministic-transition`: the
  two exits from interviewed have different triggers.
- `dead-end-state` names offered and rejected. rejected is final. offered is the planted
  gap (trap 7).
- `unhandled-event` fires (every trigger is named from one state only); it is expected
  and not graded.
- A second machine on Expense Claim (approved, returned, rejected) is acceptable but not
  expected; the graded machine is Application.

## Instances and conformance

Boulder Warehouse Crew : Team. Every attribute name on the instance (`lead`, `size`,
`members`) exists on Team. `size = 6` matches the six listed members. Outcome:
conformant, no `nonconformant-instance`. `view:object/team` renders it as
`Boulder Warehouse Crew : Team` with its three values.

## Flow clusters and default views

- hiring.md: one cluster, keyed on the document
  ([flow clusters](../docs/compiler/model/view.md#level-views)): `hiring`, titled by the
  document, with every stage change a member. The actors (Candidate, Recruiter, Hiring
  Manager) are read off the members and draw as stick figures. It yields
  `view:usecase/hiring` and `view:sequence/hiring` over the members that carry an edge.
- expenses.md: one cluster, `expenses`, with the submit and resubmit steps at least. The
  two `failure-mode` steps (missing receipt, non-business line) are members, so no
  `unrepresented-failure-mode`.
- Structural defaults are level views, one per node with two or more children, the
  scope root included (docs/compiler/model/view.md#level-views); members are the direct
  children plus every outside entity with a lifted edge into the level, no `query`.
  - `view:component/public` (one scope expected), the scope root's level view under
    the per-scope id: the parentless entities, Ridgeline Outfitters beside Employee,
    Manager, Candidate, Hiring Manager, Team, Application, Expense Claim, and the
    Employee Handbook, never "every entity" (the departments sit in Ridgeline
    Outfitters' level). Kind `component` because the parentless actors (Candidate,
    Hiring Manager, Employee, Manager) carry `actor`; `view:class/public` with the
    same members when no parentless entity carries a structural stereotype. Both are
    mechanism-faithful.
  - `view:class/ridgeline-outfitters`: the four departments (the node's children) plus
    the outside entities whose edges lift into the level: Employee (associated to a
    Department), Manager (forwards to Finance), Team when it sits outside (a Department
    composes Team). Kind `class` unless a department carries a structural stereotype.
  - `view:class/<department>` for each department with two or more children (its two
    roles, and Team or Boulder Warehouse Crew when parented there):
    `view:class/operations`, `view:class/sales`, `view:class/finance`,
    `view:class/people`. Members: the roles plus lifted interactors (Candidate and
    Application into People through the Recruiter; Employee into Finance through the
    reimbursement).
  - Deeper flow views cluster the behavior requirements that lift into a level under
    `view:usecase/<node-slug>-<doc-stem>` and `view:sequence/...`
    (`view:usecase/ridgeline-outfitters-expenses` when the expenses steps lift into the
    departments' level). The root form keeps the unprefixed ids above.
    Mechanism-faithful surplus, not graded.
- `view:state/application`, `view:object/team`.
- No timing view derives (timing views are curated). The time bounds in hiring.md
  ("within 5 business days of the application") are what a curated timing view over
  Application would read.

## Planted traps

1. Cross-doc identity: `Employee` is defined in departments.md and used in hiring.md,
   expenses.md, policies.md. ONE entity with mentions in at least 3 documents. The same
   for `Manager` (departments.md, hiring.md, expenses.md, policies.md).
2. Lookalike pair: departments.md and expenses.md say "Finance"; policies.md says "the
   Finance department" throughout. Expect reuse of `ent:finance` with the alias, or a
   merge or `duplicate-entity` diagnostic. Two surviving nodes is the failure.
3. Contradiction: expenses.md says Finance approves claims above 500 dollars;
   policies.md says above 250 dollars, for the same approval. Expect exactly one
   `contradiction` diagnostic naming both requirements, on Expense Claim or Finance.
4. Non-normative trap: hiring.md "Background" is history and hides one rule ("No offer
   goes out before People has approved the salary band for the role."). Marking the
   section non-normative must trigger `suspicious-non-normative`; extracting the rule
   and marking the section covered is also correct.
5. Junk bait: form numbers (HR-04, EX-12, HR-21), paths (`People/Hiring/Requisitions/`,
   `S:\Finance\Claims\<year>\<employee>`), policy numbers (POL-101 to POL-107), cost
   center codes (`CC-4410`), the careers URL. None of these may become entities. The
   README's rule that the handbook never mentions them is a requirement on the handbook.
6. Genuinely non-normative: policies.md "Glossary" defines outside-world terms only and
   must be marked non-normative without a `suspicious-non-normative` finding.
7. Dead end: hiring.md lists hired as a stage, but no sentence moves an application into
   it (offered → hired on the candidate accepting is the deliberately missing
   transition). `sm:application` has no hired state, offered has no exit, and
   `dead-end-state` names it. Inventing the transition from the stage list is wrong;
   the gap is for the document owner to close.
8. Quality without a measure: policies.md "Sales answers every customer email promptly."
   is a `quality` facet with no `measure` and draws `quality-unmeasured`. Every other
   quality rule in policies.md carries its bound as `measure` (10 days, 2 days per week,
   8 direct reports, 30 days, once per quarter, 2 business days).

## Diagrams

- The root level (`view:component/public`): the parentless entities, actors as
  `actor`, the rest as `component`. Ridgeline Outfitters with its lifted arrows (the
  departments' composition of Team lifts to the company:
  `"Ridgeline Outfitters" *-- "1..*" Team` when Team is parentless,
  `"Ridgeline Outfitters" -- Employee` from the Employee-to-Department association);
  Manager generalizes Employee; Employee associated to Manager. When the root derives as
  `class/public`, Team draws as a class with `lead`, `size`, `members`. Instances
  (Boulder Warehouse Crew, Dana) are absent from every level view. Ridgeline
  Outfitters' element carries the drill-down link
  `[[../class/ridgeline-outfitters.svg]]`.
- The company's level (`view:class/ridgeline-outfitters`): the four departments as
  classes, each composed of its roles and of Team (`1..*`) as lifted arrows to the
  department, plus the lifted interactors (Employee, Manager). A department with two or
  more children carries its link down to `view:class/<department>`, where the roles
  draw as classes with the department's own arrows.
- Object (`view:object/team`): one object `Boulder Warehouse Crew : Team` with
  `lead = Priya Natarajan`, `size = 6`, `members = ...`.
- No separate component view: the per-root component view of earlier designs folded
  into the level rule, and no entity here carries a structural stereotype unless the
  compile records the actors as such (then the levels holding them derive as
  `component` views with the same members).
- State (`view:state/application`): `[*] --> applied`, six arrows, the offered arrow
  labeled with its trigger and `[both references check out]`, no arrow leaving offered,
  no hired node.
- Use case and sequence per cluster: hiring shows Candidate (and the recruiter, panel,
  hiring manager as participants); expenses shows messages employee → manager,
  manager → Finance, Finance → employee.
docs/README.md:
# Ridgeline Outfitters

Ridgeline Outfitters is an outdoor gear retailer with about 120 employees, a warehouse in
Boulder, and four stores along the Front Range. These documents describe how the company
is organized and how its everyday processes work. They are the source of the Ridgeline
employee handbook.

## The company

Ridgeline Outfitters is made up of four departments:

- [Operations](departments.md#operations), which runs the warehouse and the stores.
- [Sales](departments.md#sales), which owns revenue and the wholesale accounts.
- [Finance](departments.md#finance), which keeps the books and runs payroll.
- [People](departments.md#people), which hires and supports employees.

Every department has a head. The head of a department is a manager.

## The handbook

The employee handbook is delivered as a set of markdown pages, one page per document in
this folder, under `handbook/`:

```
handbook/
  README.md
  departments.md
  hiring.md
  expenses.md
  policies.md
```

Each handbook page keeps the headings of its source document. The handbook opens with a
table of contents that links every page. A handbook page never mentions a form number or
a file path; those live in the intranet, not in the handbook.

## Documents

- [Departments](departments.md): the four departments, their roles, and their teams.
- [Hiring](hiring.md): how an application moves from applied to hired or rejected.
- [Expenses](expenses.md): how an employee gets reimbursed for money spent on company
  business.
- [Policies](policies.md): the rules that apply to every employee, and a glossary.
docs/departments.md:
# Departments

Ridgeline Outfitters has four departments: Operations, Sales, Finance, and People. This
document lists what each one does, the roles inside it, and its teams.

## Employees and managers

Every employee belongs to exactly one department. Every employee has exactly one manager.
A manager is an employee with direct reports.

## Teams

Every department is organized into one or more teams. A team has a lead, a size, and a
list of members. The lead of a team is a manager. The size of a team is the number of its
members.

## Operations

Operations runs the Boulder warehouse and the four stores. Operations receives every
shipment from a supplier, counts it in, and moves it to the store that ordered it.

Operations has two roles:

- Store Manager: runs one store, schedules its staff, and owns its shrinkage number.
- Warehouse Associate: receives shipments, picks online orders, and counts stock.

### Operations teams

The Boulder Warehouse Crew is a team in Operations. Its lead is Priya Natarajan, its size
is 6, and its members are Priya Natarajan, Tomas Reyes, Ada Okafor, Lin Zhou, Marcus
Bell, and Jo Sato.

## Sales

Sales owns the revenue target of each store and every wholesale account. Sales sets the
price list for wholesale accounts once per year.

Sales has two roles:

- Sales Associate: helps customers on the floor and rings up sales at the register.
- Account Manager: manages wholesale accounts and negotiates their pricing.

## Finance

Finance keeps the books, runs payroll, and reimburses expense claims. Finance closes the
books within 5 business days after the end of each month. Payroll runs on the 25th of
each month.

Finance has two roles:

- Accountant: keeps the ledger and closes the month.
- Payroll Specialist: runs payroll and answers pay questions.

## People

People recruits, onboards, and supports employees. People owns the hiring pipeline
described in [Hiring](hiring.md).

People has two roles:

- Recruiter: runs the hiring pipeline for every open role.
- People Partner: answers benefits and policy questions from employees.
docs/expenses.md:
# Expenses

An employee who spends their own money on company business files an expense claim to get
it back. Finance reimburses approved claims through payroll.

## The claim

An expense claim carries a total and a cost center. An expense claim carries one receipt
for every line. A claim covers purchases from a single calendar month.

Claims are filed on form EX-12 in the expense tool. Scanned receipts are stored under
`S:\Finance\Claims\<year>\<employee>`. Cost centers use the codes from the ledger, for
example `CC-4410` for the Boulder warehouse.

## Steps

1. The employee submits the expense claim to their manager with a receipt attached to
   every line.
2. The manager reviews the claim and either approves it or returns it to the employee.
3. The approvals a claim needs depend on its total:

   | Claim total          | Approvals needed                |
   | -------------------- | ------------------------------- |
   | 500 dollars or less  | the manager                     |
   | above 500 dollars    | the manager, then Finance       |

4. When the claim total is above 500 dollars, the manager forwards the approved claim to
   Finance for its approval.
5. Finance reimburses an approved claim in the next payroll run.
6. If a receipt is missing, the manager returns the claim to the employee, and the
   employee resubmits it with the receipt within 10 business days.
7. If Finance finds a line that is not a business expense, Finance rejects the claim and
   tells both the employee and the manager why.

## Timing

The manager reviews a claim within 5 business days of submission. Finance reviews a claim
it receives within 5 business days.

## Example

Dana, a sales associate, files a claim for 620 dollars after a trade show. Dana's manager
approves it on Tuesday, forwards it to Finance on the same day, and Finance approves it
on Thursday. The claim is paid in the payroll run on the 25th.
docs/hiring.md:
# Hiring

People runs hiring. A hiring manager opens a requisition for a role on form HR-04, and
the recruiter runs the pipeline below for every application against that requisition.
Requisitions are filed under `People/Hiring/Requisitions/` on the shared drive.

## Who is involved

- The candidate is a person outside the company who applied for an open role.
- The recruiter is the People role that owns the pipeline.
- The hiring manager is the manager the open role reports to.
- The interview panel is two or three employees the hiring manager picks for the loop.

## Stages

An application is in exactly one stage at a time. The stages are:

- applied: the candidate submitted the application through the careers page at
  `ridgeline.example/careers`.
- screened: the recruiter has finished the phone screen.
- interviewed: the interview panel has finished the loop.
- offered: an offer letter is with the candidate.
- hired: the candidate is on the payroll.
- rejected: the application is closed and the candidate has been told.

## Moving between stages

- An applied application becomes screened when the recruiter completes the phone screen
  with the candidate.
- An applied application becomes rejected when the recruiter finds no match at the phone
  screen.
- A screened application becomes interviewed when the interview panel completes the loop
  with the candidate.
- A screened application becomes rejected when the interview panel declines to run a
  loop.
- An interviewed application becomes offered when the hiring manager decides to hire,
  provided both of the candidate's references check out.
- An interviewed application becomes rejected when the hiring manager decides not to
  hire.

The recruiter records every stage change with its date and the person who made it. The
recruiter tells the candidate about every stage change within 2 business days.

## Timing

The recruiter completes the phone screen within 5 business days of the application. The
hiring manager decides within 3 business days of the loop. An offer stays open for 7
calendar days.

## Background

Ridgeline hired its first recruiter in 2019, when the company passed fifty employees.
Before that, store managers hired their own staff and kept the paperwork in a binder at
the Pearl Street store. The pipeline in this document replaced the binder in 2021, and
the tracker replaced a spreadsheet the year after. No offer goes out before People has
approved the salary band for the role. The salary bands themselves are reviewed every
spring.
docs/policies.md:
# Policies

These policies apply to every employee. Each policy has a number on the intranet
(POL-101 and so on); the number is a filing label, not part of the rule.

## Time off (POL-101)

Every employee takes at least 10 days of paid time off per year. An employee requests
time off on form HR-21 at least 5 business days ahead. A manager answers a time-off
request within 2 business days.

## Remote work (POL-102)

An employee works remotely at most 2 days per week. A warehouse associate works on site
every day. A sales associate works on site every day.

## Span of control (POL-103)

A manager has at most 8 direct reports.

## Spending (POL-104)

An expense claim above 250 dollars needs the Finance department's approval in addition
to the manager's approval. The Finance department pays no claim without a receipt for
every line.

## Safety (POL-105)

Every employee completes the safety training within 30 days of their start date. Every
store and the warehouse runs a fire drill once per quarter.

## Customer service (POL-106)

Sales answers every customer email promptly. A sales associate greets every customer
who enters the store.

## Benefits (POL-107)

The People department answers a benefits question within 2 business days.

## Glossary

These terms appear in the handbook with their ordinary meaning:

- Business day: a weekday that is not a public holiday.
- Calendar day: any day, weekends and holidays included.
- Cost center: the accounting bucket a purchase is charged to.
- Per diem: a fixed daily allowance for meals while traveling, a term borrowed from
  accounting.
- Shrinkage: the retail term for stock lost to theft, damage, or miscounting.
- Wholesale: selling goods in bulk to another business rather than to a consumer.

.jazyk/diagrams/state/expense-claim.puml:
@startuml
state "approved or returned" as approved_or_returned
state "forwarded to Finance" as forwarded_to_finance
[*] --> created
approved --> reimbursed : Finance reimburses through payroll
submitted --> approved_or_returned : manager reviews the claim
submitted --> approved : manager approves the claim [claim total is 500 dollars or less]
submitted --> approved : manager and Finance approve the claim [claim total is above 500 dollars]
approved --> forwarded_to_finance : manager forwards the approved claim to Finance [claim total is above 500 dollars]
approved --> reimbursed : Finance reimburses the approved claim in the next payroll run
submitted --> returned : receipt is missing
forwarded_to_finance --> rejected : Finance finds a line that is not a business expense
approved --> paid : payroll run on the 25th
created --> filed : employee spends their own money on company business
created --> filed : filed on form EX-12 in the expense tool
filed --> submitted : employee submits the expense claim to their manager [receipt attached to every line]
@enduml

.jazyk/docs/docs/README.md.yaml:
contentHash: 5f58164564f2be00
sections:
  /ridgeline-outfitters:
    title: Ridgeline Outfitters
    kind: root
    order: 0
    raw: |
      # Ridgeline Outfitters

      Ridgeline Outfitters is an outdoor gear retailer with about 120 employees, a warehouse in
      Boulder, and four stores along the Front Range. These documents describe how the company
      is organized and how its everyday processes work. They are the source of the Ridgeline
      employee handbook.
    hash: 962c7c266652759d
    lines:
    - 0
    - 7
  /ridgeline-outfitters/documents:
    title: Documents
    kind: heading
    order: 2
    parent: /ridgeline-outfitters
    raw: |-
      ## Documents

      - [Departments](departments.md): the four departments, their roles, and their teams.
      - [Hiring](hiring.md): how an application moves from applied to hired or rejected.
      - [Expenses](expenses.md): how an employee gets reimbursed for money spent on company
        business.
      - [Policies](policies.md): the rules that apply to every employee, and a glossary.
    hash: 42774ca811e8ceb5
    lines:
    - 36
    - 43
  /ridgeline-outfitters/the-company:
    title: The company
    kind: heading
    order: 0
    parent: /ridgeline-outfitters
    raw: |
      ## The company

      Ridgeline Outfitters is made up of four departments:

      - [Operations](departments.md#operations), which runs the warehouse and the stores.
      - [Sales](departments.md#sales), which owns revenue and the wholesale accounts.
      - [Finance](departments.md#finance), which keeps the books and runs payroll.
      - [People](departments.md#people), which hires and supports employees.

      Every department has a head. The head of a department is a manager.
    hash: d0335422a4573e8e
    lines:
    - 7
    - 18
  /ridgeline-outfitters/the-handbook:
    title: The handbook
    kind: heading
    order: 1
    parent: /ridgeline-outfitters
    raw: |
      ## The handbook

      The employee handbook is delivered as a set of markdown pages, one page per document in
      this folder, under `handbook/`:

      ```
      handbook/
        README.md
        departments.md
        hiring.md
        expenses.md
        policies.md
      ```

      Each handbook page keeps the headings of its source document. The handbook opens with a
      table of contents that links every page. A handbook page never mentions a form number or
      a file path; those live in the intranet, not in the handbook.
    hash: dcaf2d6322ec51d1
    lines:
    - 18
    - 36

sections:
  /departments:
    title: Departments
    kind: root
    order: 0
    raw: |
      # Departments

      Ridgeline Outfitters has four departments: Operations, Sales, Finance, and People. This
      document lists what each one does, the roles inside it, and its teams.
    hash: 92e90999ce1a83f7
    lines:
    - 0
    - 5
  /departments/employees-and-managers:
    title: Employees and managers
    kind: heading
    order: 0
    parent: /departments
    raw: |
      ## Employees and managers

      Every employee belongs to exactly one department. Every employee has exactly one manager.
      A manager is an employee with direct reports.
    hash: a56ae05da4723613
    lines:
    - 5
    - 10
  /departments/finance:
    title: Finance
    kind: heading
    order: 4
    parent: /departments
    raw: |
      ## Finance

      Finance keeps the books, runs payroll, and reimburses expense claims. Finance closes the
      books within 5 business days after the end of each month. Payroll runs on the 25th of
      each month.

      Finance has two roles:

      - Accountant: keeps the ledger and closes the month.
      - Payroll Specialist: runs payroll and answers pay questions.
    hash: 64b99c6269b76b64
    lines:
    - 42
    - 53
  /departments/operations:
    title: Operations
    kind: heading
    order: 2
    parent: /departments
    raw: |
      ## Operations

      Operations runs the Boulder warehouse and the four stores. Operations receives every
      shipment from a supplier, counts it in, and moves it to the store that ordered it.

      Operations has two roles:

      - Store Manager: runs one store, schedules its staff, and owns its shrinkage number.
      - Warehouse Associate: receives shipments, picks online orders, and counts stock.
    hash: b3ade032d7505f7d
    lines:
    - 16
    - 26
  /departments/operations/operations-teams:
    title: Operations teams
    kind: heading
    order: 0
    parent: /departments/operations
    raw: |
      ### Operations teams

      The Boulder Warehouse Crew is a team in Operations. Its lead is Priya Natarajan, its size
      is 6, and its members are Priya Natarajan, Tomas Reyes, Ada Okafor, Lin Zhou, Marcus
      Bell, and Jo Sato.
    hash: d71d9b3d2590da9e
    lines:
    - 26
    - 32
  /departments/people:
    title: People
    kind: heading
    order: 5
    parent: /departments
    raw: |-
      ## People

      People recruits, onboards, and supports employees. People owns the hiring pipeline
      described in [Hiring](hiring.md).

      People has two roles:

      - Recruiter: runs the hiring pipeline for every open role.
      - People Partner: answers benefits and policy questions from employees.
    hash: 4352c8abc362b204
    lines:
    - 53
    - 62
  /departments/sales:
    title: Sales
    kind: heading
    order: 3
    parent: /departments
    raw: |
      ## Sales

      Sales owns the revenue target of each store and every wholesale account. Sales sets the
      price list for wholesale accounts once per year.

      Sales has two roles:

      - Sales Associate: helps customers on the floor and rings up sales at the register.
      - Account Manager: manages wholesale accounts and negotiates their pricing.
    hash: 65b427eee8589f6c
    lines:
    - 32
    - 42
  /departments/teams:
    title: Teams
    kind: heading
    order: 1
    parent: /departments
    raw: |
      ## Teams

      Every department is organized into one or more teams. A team has a lead, a size, and a
      list of members. The lead of a team is a manager. The size of a team is the number of its
      members.
    hash: 1247eea3edd32a4b
    lines:
    - 10
    - 16

contentHash: 7c6916c04516e771
sections:
  /expenses:
    title: Expenses
    kind: root
    order: 0
    raw: |
      # Expenses

      An employee who spends their own money on company business files an expense claim to get
      it back. Finance reimburses approved claims through payroll.
    hash: 5d51629ad592cb0d
    lines:
    - 0
    - 5
  /expenses/example:
    title: Example
    kind: heading
    order: 3
    parent: /expenses
    raw: |-
      ## Example

      Dana, a sales associate, files a claim for 620 dollars after a trade show. Dana's manager
      approves it on Tuesday, forwards it to Finance on the same day, and Finance approves it
      on Thursday. The claim is paid in the payroll run on the 25th.
    hash: fa5e6686f1730fa0
    lines:
    - 39
    - 44
  /expenses/steps:
    title: Steps
    kind: heading
    order: 1
    parent: /expenses
    raw: |
      ## Steps

      1. The employee submits the expense claim to their manager with a receipt attached to
         every line.
      2. The manager reviews the claim and either approves it or returns it to the employee.
      3. The approvals a claim needs depend on its total:

         | Claim total          | Approvals needed                |
         | -------------------- | ------------------------------- |
         | 500 dollars or less  | the manager                     |
         | above 500 dollars    | the manager, then Finance       |

      4. When the claim total is above 500 dollars, the manager forwards the approved claim to
         Finance for its approval.
      5. Finance reimburses an approved claim in the next payroll run.
      6. If a receipt is missing, the manager returns the claim to the employee, and the
         employee resubmits it with the receipt within 10 business days.
      7. If Finance finds a line that is not a business expense, Finance rejects the claim and
         tells both the employee and the manager why.
    hash: d6b9c137bce4a803
    lines:
    - 14
    - 34
  /expenses/the-claim:
    title: The claim
    kind: heading
    order: 0
    parent: /expenses
    raw: |
      ## The claim

      An expense claim carries a total and a cost center. An expense claim carries one receipt
      for every line. A claim covers purchases from a single calendar month.

      Claims are filed on form EX-12 in the expense tool. Scanned receipts are stored under
      `S:\Finance\Claims\<year>\<employee>`. Cost centers use the codes from the ledger, for
      example `CC-4410` for the Boulder warehouse.
    hash: 0046af9c47794678
    lines:
    - 5
    - 14
  /expenses/timing:
    title: Timing
    kind: heading
    order: 2
    parent: /expenses
    raw: |
      ## Timing

      The manager reviews a claim within 5 business days of submission. Finance reviews a claim
      it receives within 5 business days.
    hash: 5669e7d1199c8155
    lines:
    - 34
    - 39

contentHash: aeafd9e12a36ec20
sections:
  /hiring:
    title: Hiring
    kind: root
    order: 0
    raw: |
      # Hiring

      People runs hiring. A hiring manager opens a requisition for a role on form HR-04, and
      the recruiter runs the pipeline below for every application against that requisition.
      Requisitions are filed under `People/Hiring/Requisitions/` on the shared drive.
    hash: 77ac3dce84cb7167
    lines:
    - 0
    - 6
  /hiring/background:
    title: Background
    kind: heading
    order: 4
    parent: /hiring
    raw: |-
      ## Background

      Ridgeline hired its first recruiter in 2019, when the company passed fifty employees.
      Before that, store managers hired their own staff and kept the paperwork in a binder at
      the Pearl Street store. The pipeline in this document replaced the binder in 2021, and
      the tracker replaced a spreadsheet the year after. No offer goes out before People has
      approved the salary band for the role. The salary bands themselves are reviewed every
      spring.
    hash: 034351eb35e2966e
    lines:
    - 49
    - 57
  /hiring/moving-between-stages:
    title: Moving between stages
    kind: heading
    order: 2
    parent: /hiring
    raw: |
      ## Moving between stages

      - An applied application becomes screened when the recruiter completes the phone screen
        with the candidate.
      - An applied application becomes rejected when the recruiter finds no match at the phone
        screen.
      - A screened application becomes interviewed when the interview panel completes the loop
        with the candidate.
      - A screened application becomes rejected when the interview panel declines to run a
        loop.
      - An interviewed application becomes offered when the hiring manager decides to hire,
        provided both of the candidate's references check out.
      - An interviewed application becomes rejected when the hiring manager decides not to
        hire.

      The recruiter records every stage change with its date and the person who made it. The
      recruiter tells the candidate about every stage change within 2 business days.
    hash: c1905c6f9c6e56e6
    lines:
    - 25
    - 43
  /hiring/stages:
    title: Stages
    kind: heading
    order: 1
    parent: /hiring
    raw: |
      ## Stages

      An application is in exactly one stage at a time. The stages are:

      - applied: the candidate submitted the application through the careers page at
        `ridgeline.example/careers`.
      - screened: the recruiter has finished the phone screen.
      - interviewed: the interview panel has finished the loop.
      - offered: an offer letter is with the candidate.
      - hired: the candidate is on the payroll.
      - rejected: the application is closed and the candidate has been told.
    hash: 4a67a5e3480951cb
    lines:
    - 13
    - 25
  /hiring/timing:
    title: Timing
    kind: heading
    order: 3
    parent: /hiring
    raw: |
      ## Timing

      The recruiter completes the phone screen within 5 business days of the application. The
      hiring manager decides within 3 business days of the loop. An offer stays open for 7
      calendar days.
    hash: 88cd4db4c2a77cfc
    lines:
    - 43
    - 49
  /hiring/who-is-involved:
    title: Who is involved
    kind: heading
    order: 0
    parent: /hiring
    raw: |
      ## Who is involved

      - The candidate is a person outside the company who applied for an open role.
      - The recruiter is the People role that owns the pipeline.
      - The hiring manager is the manager the open role reports to.
      - The interview panel is two or three employees the hiring manager picks for the loop.
    hash: 2726d4f776fc0a70
    lines:
    - 6
    - 13

.jazyk/docs/docs/policies.md.yaml:
contentHash: 9e9be57ac1b053b5
sections:
  /policies:
    title: Policies
    kind: root
    order: 0
    raw: |
      # Policies

      These policies apply to every employee. Each policy has a number on the intranet
      (POL-101 and so on); the number is a filing label, not part of the rule.
    hash: 8a597068d23b44bc
    lines:
    - 0
    - 5
  /policies/benefits-pol-107:
    title: Benefits (POL-107)
    kind: heading
    order: 6
    parent: /policies
    raw: |
      ## Benefits (POL-107)

      The People department answers a benefits question within 2 business days.
    hash: 1950d940fdfeace6
    lines:
    - 36
    - 40
  /policies/customer-service-pol-106:
    title: Customer service (POL-106)
    kind: heading
    order: 5
    parent: /policies
    raw: |
      ## Customer service (POL-106)

      Sales answers every customer email promptly. A sales associate greets every customer
      who enters the store.
    hash: 5ace6bc7410ad5b5
    lines:
    - 31
    - 36
  /policies/glossary:
    title: Glossary
    kind: heading
    order: 7
    parent: /policies
    raw: |-
      ## Glossary

      These terms appear in the handbook with their ordinary meaning:

      - Business day: a weekday that is not a public holiday.
      - Calendar day: any day, weekends and holidays included.
      - Cost center: the accounting bucket a purchase is charged to.
      - Per diem: a fixed daily allowance for meals while traveling, a term borrowed from
        accounting.
      - Shrinkage: the retail term for stock lost to theft, damage, or miscounting.
      - Wholesale: selling goods in bulk to another business rather than to a consumer.
    hash: 75cec08b947c4977
    lines:
    - 40
    - 51
  /policies/remote-work-pol-102:
    title: Remote work (POL-102)
    kind: heading
    order: 1
    parent: /policies
    raw: |
      ## Remote work (POL-102)

      An employee works remotely at most 2 days per week. A warehouse associate works on site
      every day. A sales associate works on site every day.
    hash: c312005f929bb1d0
    lines:
    - 11
    - 16
  /policies/safety-pol-105:
    title: Safety (POL-105)
    kind: heading
    order: 4
    parent: /policies
    raw: |
      ## Safety (POL-105)

      Every employee completes the safety training within 30 days of their start date. Every
      store and the warehouse runs a fire drill once per quarter.
    hash: 864bc936d0e2ebb5
    lines:
    - 26
    - 31
  /policies/span-of-control-pol-103:
    title: Span of control (POL-103)
    kind: heading
    order: 2
    parent: /policies

  severity: info
  subjects:
  - req:departments-17
  - req:readme-6
  message: Both requirements state that Sales owns revenue and wholesale accounts; both are kept because they come from different documents.
  reasoning: The departments quote says Sales owns the revenue target of each store and every wholesale account, while the README quote says Sales owns revenue and the wholesale accounts. This is intentional cross-document redundancy rather than an in-document duplicate.

    question: Keep both cross-document Sales ownership statements?
    options:
    - label: Keep both

    freeform: true
  created: g16
  updated: g16

ent:application:
  name: Application
  definition: A candidate's application against a requisition in the hiring pipeline.
  stereotype: record
  mentions:
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring
    quote: the recruiter runs the pipeline below for every application against that requisition.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/stages
    quote: 'An application is in exactly one stage at a time. The stages are:'
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/stages
    quote: |-
      - applied: the candidate submitted the application through the careers page at
        `ridgeline.example/careers`.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/stages
    quote: '- screened: the recruiter has finished the phone screen.'
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/stages
    quote: '- interviewed: the interview panel has finished the loop.'
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/stages
    quote: '- offered: an offer letter is with the candidate.'
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/stages
    quote: '- hired: the candidate is on the payroll.'
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/stages
    quote: '- rejected: the application is closed and the candidate has been told.'
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/moving-between-stages
    quote: |-
      - An applied application becomes screened when the recruiter completes the phone screen
        with the candidate.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/moving-between-stages
    quote: |-
      - An applied application becomes rejected when the recruiter finds no match at the phone
        screen.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/moving-between-stages
    quote: |-
      - A screened application becomes interviewed when the interview panel completes the loop
        with the candidate.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/moving-between-stages
    quote: |-
      - A screened application becomes rejected when the interview panel declines to run a
        loop.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/moving-between-stages
    quote: |-
      - An interviewed application becomes offered when the hiring manager decides to hire,
        provided both of the candidate's references check out.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/moving-between-stages
    quote: |-
      - An interviewed application becomes rejected when the hiring manager decides not to
        hire.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/moving-between-stages
    quote: The recruiter records every stage change with its date and the person who made it.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/moving-between-stages
    quote: |-
      The
      recruiter tells the candidate about every stage change within 2 business days.
  - doc: docs/hiring.md
    section: /hiring/timing
    quote: The recruiter completes the phone screen within 5 business days of the application.
  created: g10
  updated: g11
